new: Sharp text is on by default in Quest Browser. The story's text panel and play bar are drawn by the headset itself, at the display's resolution.
The default is layer, the cheapest. It sits behind the scene, so rays, labels and the menu still show over the panel.
The Debug tab also offers for text (the headset's text filter, more work every frame), in front (covers rays and menu) and off. In front starts with the next session.
Other browsers start with it off. If VR ever closes by itself with Sharp text on, the next session starts without it; the Debug tab says so.
Notebook pictures in a headset show the story panel: Sharp text pauses for a moment while one is taken.
test: On a Quest in VR and AR, without touching the Debug tab: the story panel should be sharp from the first session.
Point at the panel's buttons: the ray and its dot show over the panel. Open the menu in front of the panel.
Swap stories, open the Stories screen and explore mode, try Cards in 3D and on top, and move the panel with the grip.
Take a notebook note with the panel in view: the picture should show the panel.
Watch the frame rate with Sharp text on and off (the Debug tab's line shows how long a write takes).
untested: Other headsets and browsers (a Pico, Wolvic): off there; turned on, the panel's size is unchecked.
The fallbacks (VR closing by itself, a failing layer, the notebook's pause): tried only with a pretend headset.
The cost of Sharp text on a Quest at 90 Hz.
In AR, a real hand in front of the panel does not hide it.
